title: Ultrasound of the liver and gallbladder
what: The doctor looks at your liver, gallbladder, and bile ducts with ultrasound. It is safe, with no radiation.
why: For pain on the right side under the ribs, abnormal liver blood tests, or possible gallstones or fatty liver.
tell_doctor: If your gallbladder has been removed
If you recently had a gastroscopy or colonoscopy. Air may still be in your bowel

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: No food for 6 to 8 hours. After eating, the gallbladder shrinks and is hard to see. The scan is usually done in the morning before breakfast.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: A light dinner without fizzy drinks, raw vegetables, beans, or dark rye bread. Less gas means a clearer view.

prepare.title: Water
prepare.text: A little water is fine. If your clinic suggests an anti-gas medicine, take it as they say.

bring: Past ultrasound reports, if you have them
A tissue or towel to wipe off the gel
steps: You lie on your back with your belly uncovered
The doctor puts on a cool gel
The probe moves over the right side of your belly, under the ribs
You will be asked to take a deep breath and hold it for a few seconds
Sometimes you are asked to turn onto your left side
feel: The probe presses a little. It does not hurt
after: The gel is wiped off, and you can eat right away
The report is usually given right away

faq.q: Why must I come hungry for a liver ultrasound?
faq.a: After eating, the gallbladder shrinks, and the doctor cannot see stones. So no food for 6 to 8 hours.
Yes, it often can. To check how stiff the liver is, a scan called elastography is sometimes added.

reminders.text: Liver ultrasound tomorrow. Have a light dinner with no fizzy drinks, beans, or raw vegetables.
Stop eating now until your ultrasound. A little water is fine.
